headline: DILG, DepEd Outline School Security Upgrades as ₱5-Billion Plan Is Proposed
seoTitle: DILG, DepEd Outline School Security Upgrades | FMB News
seoDescription: DILG and DepEd are moving to strengthen school security through tighter access controls, surveillance and mental-health support, while an approved FMB News brief reports a proposed ₱5-billion modernization package.
deck: Government agencies are tightening school-security coordination after recent campus violence, with surveillance, access control and student-support measures under discussion.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: The Department of the Interior and Local Government and the Department of Education are advancing a broader school-security program following recent campus violence.

The approved FMB News newsroom brief reports that agencies are proposing a ₱5-billion modernization package for public-school security. FMB News could independently confirm the policy direction toward stronger surveillance, metal detectors, closer law-enforcement coordination and student-support measures, but not the exact ₱5-billion package from an official same-day primary document.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: DILG said on August 20 that it and DepEd were preparing an agreement to strengthen security inside school premises, including possible barangay-tanod stations in schools. A current government information report also says DepEd is seeking stronger surveillance through CCTV installations and metal detectors while emphasizing learner well-being and inter-agency partnerships.

The newsroom brief further attributes proposed electronic screening, panic-alert links and expanded mental-health support to the developing 2027 security plan. Those specific funding components remain attributed to the approved brief pending a retrievable official budget document.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: School security measures can reduce response time and improve access control, but hardware alone does not address warning signs, student distress or the risk of creating a climate of fear. The strongest policy mix combines proportionate physical safeguards with trained personnel, reporting pathways and mental-health support.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch DILG, DepEd and Congress for the signed inter-agency agreement, the formal 2027 budget submission, any itemized appropriation supporting the reported ₱5-billion figure, and implementation standards for CCTV, metal detectors, emergency alerts and psychosocial support.
